correctness.rationale: For a three-generated CI gluing S=<qa,qb,p>, gcd(a,b)=gcd(p,q)=1, q>=2, a<b, p nonminimal in <a,b>, the Frobenius number is q(ab-a-b)+(q-1)p and the multiplicity is min(qa,p). Because ab-a-b>=a^2-a-1, if qa=m=s^2 then p>=m+1 gives F>=m(a+q-2)-1>=2m(s-1)-1 by AM–GM, equality only a=q=s,b=s+1,p=m+1. If p=m<qa, q>s^2/a implies a strict improvement over the same target; for a=s integer q>=s+1 yields strict inequality. The candidate p=s^2+1=(s-1)s+(s+1) is legal and achieves F=2s^2(s-1)-1; CI symmetry gives g=(F+1)/2. Independent finite gluing search confirmed uniqueness for s=2..6; those tests are not the universal proof.
residual_risks: The independent search is bounded; the universal claim rests on Delorme’s gluing theorem, symmetry, and the reviewed inequalities.

It is not a renaming of a two-generator formula: the gluing parameters require optimized global inequalities.
